items.it: Oggi al nonno gli fa male la schiena.
Il dottore gli dà una medicina e lui la prende.
items.en: The doctor gives him medicine and he takes it.

anchors: Indirect object 'gli' (to him) vs. Direct object 'la' (it, feminine).
Reflexive daily habit: alzarsi (si alza) & riposarsi (si riposa).

stage1_rawInput.title: Ciao

items.it: Oggi desidero la pace per tutti.
items.en: Today, I wish peace for everyone.

items.it: Per ogni persona in questo mondo.
items.en: For every person in this world.
Do we comfort those who are suffering?

items.it: Pregate con me per chi soffre.
items.en: Pray with me for those who are suffering.

anchors: Relative 'chi' = 'those who / anyone who' (e.g., 'chi soffre' = those who suffer, rather than a question word 'who?').
Subject-dropped Imperative ('noi' / 'voi' command): e.g., 'Siamo...' = 'Let's be...', 'Vediamo...' = 'Let's see...', 'Pregate...' = 'Pray (you all)...'.
Pre-verb Object Pronouns (S + O + V): Short pronouns like 'mi / ti / gli / le / lo / la' sit directly BEFORE the conjugated verb.
Possessive placed AFTER the noun (e.g., 'amici miei'): Used in direct greetings/vocatives for warmth and affection.
